question.problem:
Consider the vector field $F=⟨0,\,y,\,-x⟩$ and the closed surface $S$ that encloses the finite region between the cone $z=3\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-9$ and the plane $z=y-x.$ Let $D$ be the projection of $S$ onto the $xy$-plane. The flux of $F$ across $S$ can be expressed in terms of a double integral as 

$$
{∬}_{S}F\cdot dS={∬}_{D}\,\bbox[3pt,border: 1pt solid black]{\phantom{AAAAAAA}}\,\text{d}A.
$$

Which of the following could be the missing expression?
question.worked_solution:
Since we have a closed surface, the positive orientation is outward-pointing by convention. So,

- the upper surface ${S}_{1}:z=g(x,y)=y-x$ is oriented upward, and

- the lower surface ${S}_{2}:z=h(x,y)=3\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-9$ is oriented downward.

Now, we write down the flux across each of the surfaces separately.

- Consider the upper plane ${S}_{1}.$

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=g(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂g}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(y-x)=-1 \\ \frac{∂g}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(y-x)=1\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=0,\,Q=y,\,R=-x.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-0\cdot (-1)-y\cdot 1+(-x))\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-y-x)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

- Consider lower cone ${S}_{2}.$ 

We compute the partial derivatives of $z=h(x,y):$

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{∂h}{∂x} & =\frac{∂}{∂x}(3\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-9)=\frac{3x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}} \\ \frac{∂h}{∂y} & =\frac{∂}{∂y}(3\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}-9)=\frac{3y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}\end{aligned}
$$

If we denote $F=⟨P,\,Q,\,R⟩,$ then

$$
P=0,\,Q=y,\,R=-x.
$$

 

As a result, since the positive orientation is upward, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S & =-{∬}_{D}(-P\frac{∂g}{∂x}-Q\frac{∂g}{∂y}+R)\text{d}A \\  & =-{∬}_{D}(-0\cdot \frac{3x}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}-y\cdot \frac{3y}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}+(-x))\,\text{d}A \\  & =-{∬}_{D}(-\frac{3{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}-x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}(\frac{3{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}+x)\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the flux across the entire surface is 

$$
\begin{aligned}{∬}_{S}F\cdot \text{d}S & ={∬}_{{S}_{1}}F\cdot \text{d}S+{∬}_{{S}_{2}}F\cdot \text{d}S \\  & ={∬}_{D}(-y-x)\,\text{d}A+{∬}_{D}(\frac{3{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}+x)\,\text{d}A \\  & ={∬}_{D}\frac{3{y}^{2}}{\sqrt{{x}^{2}+{y}^{2}}}-y\,\text{d}A.\end{aligned}
$$
